Walleye boat anglers continued to drift hook-and-worm rigs, while shore anglers drifted jigs tipped with worms.
Freshwater drum were caught throughout the river while anglers drifted jigs tipped with worms, drifted nightcrawler harnesses, and bottom fished with drop-shot rigs.
Anglers found smallmouth bass throughout the Cheboygan River, from the Cheboygan Dam spillway to the State Street drawbridge, with additional catches reported in Duncan Bay. Anglers found success using a variety of techniques, including fishing with floating nightcrawlers and casting crankbaits, spinners, swimbaits, and tube jigs. Undersized northern pike were also caught in Duncan Bay while anglers used swimbaits.

Anglers fishing in 70 to 100 feet of water caught a fair amount of lake trout, with some nice steelhead and walleye mixed in higher in the water column. Additionally, occasional coho salmon and Atlantic salmon were also caught. Dark red and orange were good colors for spoons. A handful of walleye were caught in the lower river and mouth of the Au Sable River by anglers drifting crawlers along the bottom.

Anglers fishing in 70 to 90 feet of water found lake trout, with some larger lake trout caught deeper in 130 to 170 feet of water. Green, orange, and white Spin-N-Glos produced trout. Copper lines ranging from 50 to 150 feet with orange or green spoons produced some steelhead and the occasional Atlantic salmon. Anglers casting in the harbor caught a fair amount of northern pike while using spinnerbaits.

Anglers fished up the lake toward 40 Mile Point straight out from the harbor and south toward Adams Point. The best depths ranged from 55 to 120 feet of water. Anglers reported catching a mix of mostly lake trout, with occasional steelhead, coho salmon, walleye, and Chinook salmon. Lines were run throughout the water column.
Steelhead were caught higher in the water column using regular-sized or smaller spoons. Productive colors included orange and pink paired with silver, gold, or copper finishes. Lead cores ranging from 1 to 5 colors were effective. Other species were primarily caught on spoons, with some success reported using flashers and flies or meat rigs. Productive colors included greens, blues, chartreuse, white, and glow patterns, especially early and late in the day. Anglers trolled at faster speeds when targeting silver fish.

There was more offshore fishing activity, with anglers heading out to 180 feet of water or deeper. Anglers found success targeting lake trout, steelhead, and coho salmon, with the occasional pink salmon also being caught. Regular-sized or smaller spoons were effective, with orange patterns producing well. Anglers reported success while trolling at faster speeds and looking for bug slicks.
Fishing also remained productive closer to shore in 55 to 100 feet of water. Anglers reported a mixed bag consisting mostly of lake trout, with occasional coho salmon and Chinook salmon. Lines were run throughout the water column, with spoons being the most effective presentation. Productive colors included greens, blues, UV, chartreuse, white, pearl, and glow patterns, especially early and late in the day. Anglers trolled at faster speeds when targeting silver fish. Good fishing locations included areas straight north between the two lighthouses and south toward Stoneport and False Presque Isle.
Anglers targeting Chinook salmon found a few fish along the shelf in 80 to 115 feet of water while fishing the top 50 feet of the water column with spoons. The piers were slow.

Chinook salmon were caught out from Pentwater in 75 to 90 feet of water, straight out from the pierheads in 50 to 180 feet of water, and around Big Sable Point in 50 to 180 feet of water. Fish were caught 25 to 50 feet down, with spoons being the most productive lure. A few steelhead were also caught. Pier anglers caught several freshwater drum and a couple of suckers while casting spoons, lures, and nightcrawlers. The salmon bite was slow from the piers.

Boat anglers trolling for salmon reported scattered fish throughout the bay. Anglers who found success, caught Chinook salmon on spoons while fishing in 40 to 70 feet of water over depths greater than 100 feet. Occasional bites on meat rigs were also reported. Anglers targeting lake trout found occasional fish near the bottom while trolling between Petoskey and Big Rock, as well as while fishing the “humps” west of Harbor Springs.

Boat anglers trolling for salmon reported a fair number of fish near North Manitou Island. The best fishing occurred in 250 to 325 feet of water, with the highest catch rates around 300 feet. Anglers noted that fish were biting but many did not hook up, resulting in numerous missed fish. Many anglers had to increase trolling speed.Those who successfully caught Chinook salmon reported that dipsy diver rods produced the best results. Productive bait included green and blue spoons, as well as both natural and artificial meat rigs.
Another productive area was between the docks on North Manitou Island. Several anglers reported good success starting their troll at the north end of the island and continuing north.Water temperatures remained in the mid-60s near the surface and dropped to approximately 45 degrees at a depth of 140 feet.

Winds proved to make angling tough, pushing Chinook salmon into deeper water. Anglers reported catches in 180 to 240 feet of water while working the top 120 feet of the water column. Spoons continued to produce the most bites, but meat rigs also produced Chinook salmon. Very good numbers of lake trout were reported in Platte Bay and Six Mile Hole by anglers targeting the bottom with cow bells and Spin-N-Glos.

Fishing effort increased as more boat anglers reported fair harvest rates for lake trout. Anglers targeted lake trout while jigging near Stoney Point, Omena Bay, and the surrounding waters off Northport. Small white and gold spoons produced the best results for anglers jigging. Anglers trolling reported catching salmon in the area and noted that they marked large schools of suspended fish throughout the water column.
Fishing for panfish was great on all lakes, with multiple anglers catching limits bluegills from both the shore and boats. Pike fishing continued to be slow.

Fishing for bass and panfish was reported as good to great. Multiple anglers reported good bass fishing in the morning. Some anglers also caught limits of quality bluegills. A few pike were also reported by anglers targeting them.
Walleye fishing was good during the late evening. Bluegills and rock bass were caught in good numbers below Rogers Dam.
Fishing was very good from both kayaks and the shore. Anglers caught multiple panfish and bass, with most targeting the channels.
Smallmouth bass fishing on the Muskegon River was phenomenal. Trout fishing was slow but will hopefully pick back up in the coming weeks.

Lake Michigan fishing was great, with many anglers catching limits of Chinook salmon from Whitehall north to the Silver Lake Sand Dunes. Anglers caught a mixed bag of Chinook salmon, steelhead, coho salmon, and brown trout. A drop in water temperature brought Chinook salmon into shallower water.

Yellow perch anglers reported catching some fish near the Escanaba Harbor and the mouth of the Escanaba River. Perch fishing in the head of the bay was slow, and anglers targeting walleye had limited success. Walleye fishing was slow, with anglers trolling crawler harnesses with bottom bouncers. Walleye anglers targeted deeper water along the bottoms of drop-offs. Some anglers reported catching eater-sized walleye near weed beds. Smallmouth bass anglers targeted rocky areas near steep drop-offs or flats adjacent to deep water.
Boating anglers trolling and jigging picked up a few lake trout around Grand Island and Wood Island. Anglers reported a slow bite for splake off the Anna River mouth.

Anglers reported fair to poor fishing for coho salmon and lake trout while trolling. Anglers used spoons and flasher/flies while trolling, but had limited success, reporting slower fishing compared to previous weeks. Anglers reported a slow to fair bite while jigging for lake trout, with most fish caught on natural presentations in waters ranging from 150 to 200 feet.

Anglers trolling near structure in 60 to 100 feet of water reported good numbers of lake trout and a few coho salmon while using spoons and flasher/flies. Anglers also reported catches of smaller Chinook salmon in low numbers. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a poor to fair bite when using natural and artificial baits, with a few fish being caught between 140 and 180 feet of water.

Angling efforts on the river remained fair over the past week. Anglers reported catching walleye in fair to good numbers. Both trolling and jigging proved to be successful methods for finding these fish. However, some anglers showed a preference for jigging. Shore anglers reported catching walleye and rock bass in low to fair numbers. Occasional catches of lake sturgeon were also reported.

Angling efforts from Ontonagon were low. Efforts from the Silver City and Union Bay access sites were even lower by comparison. Recent angler reports included catches of lake trout in low to fair numbers, along with less frequent catches of coho salmon. Trolling continued to be the preferred fishing method for boat anglers. Anglers reported catches occurring across depths ranging from 40 to 180 feet of water.

Angling efforts from the harbor were low over the past week. Anglers reported catching lake trout in low numbers. Trolling continued to be the preferred method for targeting these fish. Boat anglers had the best success while trolling across a variety of depths ranging from 40 to 180 feet of water. Shore anglers reported occasional catches of smallmouth bass and northern pike within the harbor boundaries.

At the Pine River, anglers reported catches of walleye, perch, and bullheads throughout the week. The perch bite was excellent early in the week, with anglers finding success while drifting nightcrawlers near the M-134 overpass bridge and at the mouth of the river. As the week progressed, walleye catch rates declined, with anglers reporting fewer consistent bites. Many of the walleye caught were undersized and were released, though occasional anglers were able to harvest up to three walleye. Most anglers, however, were unable to catch any keeper-sized walleye.

Boat anglers did very well targeting lake trout while trolling and jigging. A few reports of coho salmon being caught while trolling were also received. Fishing pressure off the break wall remained low.

Anglers in DeTour caught good numbers of cisco around Fairbank and Trout Island. If mayflies were in the area, the fish remained in the area as well, although they were often on the move. A walleye tournament was scheduled for Thursday and Friday, anglers pre-fished for it but had little success due to the high winds and ongoing mayfly hatches. There were reports of salmon being caught while trolling around the lighthouse, as well as lake trout caught while trolling through the flats.
In Hessel, anglers caught perch off the pier, having to sort through many small fish to find keepers. There were good numbers of bass caught around Mackinaw Bay and the Echo Islands.

Chinook salmon anglers reported fair fishing. Trolling spoons and flasher/fly combos at depths of 50 to 90 feet of water was productive. Glow lures were commonly used during low-light periods of the day. Rainbow trout and a few lake trout were also reported.

Lake trout anglers fished deeper than usual. Most anglers trolled north of White Rocks toward the area north of Granite Rock in 120 to 220 feet of water or jigged structure around White Rocks and the surrounding islands in about 140 feet of water.
Anglers began heading back out to Sand River and Shot Point, where they experienced fair success catching lake trout and brown trout in around 70 feet of water. The fish caught this week were holding deeper in the water column, unlike the previous two weeks when many fish were caught closer to the surface and were full of bugs.

Fishing in Au Train remained slow this week, only one angler was observed on the water due to the smoke and poor weather. However, he fished three times and caught his limit of lake trout on all three trips, along with a few coho salmon. He had to move to different locations each day to find fish. The lake trout appeared to be holding shallower compared to the previous three weeks, in 120 to 180 feet of water.
Most fish were holding near the bottom this week and were full of ciscoes, unlike last week when they were suspended in the water column feeding on bugs. Fishing effort remained very light.
Fishing activity increased with most anglers targeting yellow perch. Anglers had the most success in 10 to 15 feet of water using natural bait.

Floats can be a useful tool for anglers looking to find bigger fish while also producing a relaxing fishing opportunity while sitting back and letting the gear work its magic.
Using a float, such as a traditional bobber, classic teardrop or oval-shaped option, will allow fish to have time to check out your bait up close and decide if they want to take a bite.
Anglers will also need to decide between using a spring-type fixed bobber or a slip bobber. A slip bobber offers you more flexibility because it can move up and down the line — depending on where you put a stopper.
This report is intended to give you an idea of what is going on around the state. Updates come from Fisheries staff and conservation officers. With nearly 11,000 inland lakes, the Great Lakes and thousands of miles of rivers and streams, not all locations can be listed. However, it is safe to say if a species is being caught in some waters in the area, they are likely being caught in all waters in that section of the state that have that species.

Yellow perch fishing improved slightly, though overall action remained slow. Anglers caught a few perch east of Bolles Harbor in 18 feet of water using perch rigs tipped with minnows. Anglers targeting walleye found success trolling crawler harnesses east of Stony Point along the Michigan–Ohio state line. Largemouth bass fishing in the area channels was good on artificial lures, primarily soft plastics.
Walleye were caught off Finn Road in 7 to 10 feet of water while trolling with nightcrawlers. Yellow perch were caught at the Spark Plug and near the sailboat buoys.

Strong winds kept anglers off the bay over the past few days, and fishing pressure dropped off. Prior to the wind, walleye anglers did well in Sebewaing trolling Flicker Shads over the bar in 14 to 15 feet of water. Aside from that, activity was minimal.
The boat launch was partially closed, with one ramp in operation. Fishing was generally slow, as most watercraft on the lake were recreational boaters.

The bite was generally slow. Anglers had some success trolling for walleye with crawler harnesses and spoons in 100 to 120 feet of water, averaging 1 to 2 fish per boat. Lake trout and steelhead action picked up for anglers trolling spoons in 100 to 150 feet of water, with a few steelhead caught around 85 feet down. A few anglers also caught the occasional coho salmon and Atlantic salmon. Pier anglers targeting salmon had no success but did well when targeting northern pike and bass with inline spinners in the harbor.

Windy conditions throughout the week made boat fishing slow. Early in the week, anglers had success trolling spoons for walleye, steelhead, and lake trout in 100 to 140 feet of water. Pier anglers had some success targeting walleye in the harbor with jointed swimbaits.
Fishing was slow with no fish reported due to high winds. A few anglers caught smallmouth bass off the head of the pier using soft plastic baits.
Boat anglers caught salmon from the breakwalls out to 80 feet of water. Glow plugs and glow spoons worked best. Pier anglers casting glow spoons caught a few Chinook salmon.

Salmon were caught from the pierheads in 70 feet of water. Glow spoons, glow plugs, and white flies were all productive. Pier anglers caught salmon while casting glow spoons or using live bait like gizzard shad and alewives. Largemouth bass were caught on drop-shot rigs.

Strong winds kept most boat anglers off the water. Those who ventured out returned with an average of five walleye per boat. A few anglers targeted yellow perch and caught a few keepers, but no limits were reported. Largemouth bass were caught out of the Tawas River and off the state dock, though fishing overall remained slow.
Fishing activity was minimal over the past week. A few boat anglers targeted walleye in 30 to 50 feet of water, though anglers reported slow fishing with fish scattered across Thunder Bay.

Catfish were caught in good numbers from the armory up to the 9th Street Dam. Cut bait and nightcrawlers fished on the bottom were productive. A few small smallmouth bass and northern pike were caught using spinners and crankbaits. Anglers reported no success targeting walleye.

High winds reduced angler activity over the past week. Anglers had mixed results targeting walleye, with fish scattered throughout the water column in 20 to 100 feet of water. Anglers who found success reported the best results on deep-diving crankbaits in natural and green patterns.

Low numbers of salmon were reported staging at the mouth of the Cheboygan River. Anglers cast glow spoons early in the morning and late at night. Smallmouth bass and rock bass, along with the occasional northern pike, were caught between the State Street drawbridge and the Cheboygan Dam spillway. Smallmouth bass and rock bass were caught while drifting nightcrawlers, and northern pike were caught using jerkbaits.

Anglers trolling in 120 to 160 feet of water had fair lake trout fishing using spoons and Spin-N-Glos. Walleye were caught in 80 to 160 feet of water while trolling 20 to 40 feet down; small spoons and nightcrawler harnesses produced some fish. Anglers fishing from the pier and catwalk caught channel catfish using nightcrawlers on the bottom.

Anglers targeting lake trout did well in 180 to 200 feet of water while trolling spoons and Spin-N-Glos. A handful of steelhead were taken on spoons in 120 to 160 feet of water. Anglers casting spinners in the harbor reported catching a few northern pike.

Salmon arrived in good numbers, though weather conditions dictated angler activity. The most productive bites occurred at first and last light, with anglers fishing primarily off Swan Bay. Anglers deployed lead core lines of varying lengths, downriggers, dipsy divers, and copper wire to cover the entire water column. The best depths were 40 to 90 feet of water. Salmon held in shallower water early and late in the day, moving deeper during midday. Anglers used an assortment of spoons, J-Plugs, flasher-fly and squid combinations, and flashers with meat rigs. Productive colors included green, blue, chartreuse, black, white, UV white, pearl, and glow patterns. While the focus remained primarily on salmon, activity also extended north along US-23 toward 40 Mile Point.

Salmon and trout fishing remained slow, lake trout were caught deep at the hump. The most productive depths were 120 feet of water and deeper near the bottom using spoons or attractors paired with Spin-N-Glo lures or Spin-N-Glo flies. A few anglers targeted fish around Stoneport and False Presque Isle with some success. Walleye anglers did well during evening and after dark while trolling body baits or crawler harnesses. The best depths were 30 to 65 feet of water, with anglers targeting the top 35 feet.

Anglers targeting salmon found them both north and south of the port while trolling in depths from 70 to 300 feet of water. Fish were typically caught 60 to 80 feet down and at depths of 100+ feet of water. Spoons, flies, and plugs worked best in the early mornings and late evenings. At the beginning of the week, a few Chinook salmon were caught off the pier, in the channel, and in Manistee Lake. Anglers trolling in front of the pier heads also caught Chinook salmon on plugs and spoons.

Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and a few steelhead were caught straight out and south in 80 to 110 feet of water while trolling 35 feet down to the bottom, as well as northwest up toward Big Sable Point in 60 to 120 feet of water while fishing 40 to 80+ feet down or near the bottom. Plugs, spoons, and flies worked best. At the beginning of the week, Chinook salmon were caught while jigging or trolling in the harbor, in front of the piers, and in Pere Marquette Lake.

Strong northwest winds kept angling activity to a minimum. Anglers who made it out reported low numbers of salmon. The temperature break was reported at 75 to 100 feet down, with anglers finding some success trolling in 150 to 200 feet of water. Spoons and meat rigs fished in the early morning produced better results than in the evening.

Strong northwest winds kept angling activity to a minimum. Anglers who made it out reported low numbers of salmon, primarily on the north side of the bay. Boat anglers staying out of the wind reported low numbers 60 to 90 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water. Spoons and meat rigs fished in the early morning produced better results than in the evening.

Strong winds made conditions tough and limited fishing activity over the past week. Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught Chinook salmon while trolling in 110 to 140 feet of water. Water temperatures throughout the bay hovered between 70 and 73 degrees.

Strong winds made conditions tough and limited fishing activity over the past week. Anglers who got out caught a few lake trout along with an occasional Chinook salmon in 100 to 140 feet of water along the west bank just north of Elmwood Marina. Anglers trolling close to the mouth of the Boardman River also caught a few Chinook salmon, though the bite was slow. Water temperatures hovered between 69 and 73 degrees.

Boat anglers caught Chinook salmon and steelhead north of North Manitou Island while trolling in 150 to 300 feet of water with baits set 60 to 125 feet down. Green plugs, spoons, and flies produced well.
Anglers fishing around the Crib caught a few steelhead and coho salmon. A few fish moved closer to shore. Anglers trolling north along the first and second banks found success when targeting Chinook salmon. Pier anglers reported no signs of Chinook salmon yet, but caught yellow perch, bluegill, smallmouth bass, and a few catfish.

North winds rolled the lake over, bringing cooler water in. Chinook salmon responded by moving into the harbor, directly out front, and into the river. Breakwall anglers, jiggers, and open-water trollers reported strong numbers. Coho salmon also moved into Platte Bay.

With the lake rolling over, anglers fishing the Barrel and in front of the golf course reported good numbers of Chinook salmon in the early mornings, mostly on spoons, though plugs had success as well.

Boat anglers targeting Chinook salmon had some success when trolling in front of Stoney point and Belanger Creek. Lake trout anglers were successful when jigging white, gold tubes or spoons near Stoney point and in Omena Bay.

Anglers targeting yellow perch reported good fishing while using perch rigs baited with worms and minnows on light-action rods. Walleye anglers reported slow-to-fair fishing, with most targeting the bottom of drop-offs. Anglers trolling typically ran crawler harnesses behind bottom bouncers or inline weights. Anglers casting reported using snap-style jigs or jigs paired with soft plastics. Coho salmon fishing was slow over the past week.

Weather conditions limited fishing activity over the past week, but boat anglers who made it out caught a few coho salmon and splake while trolling in the bay and around Grand Island. Boat anglers targeting lake trout found success at Big Reef and around Grand Island. Anglers fishing the mouth of the Anna River caught a few splake. Spawn and casting spinners were the most productive baits.

Angling effort on the river was good over the past week. Walleye were caught in fair numbers by anglers jigging. Trolling was much less effective, with fishing in the morning hours yielding the best success.

Ontonagon saw fair amounts of angling effort over the past week. Effort from the Silver City and Union Bay access sites remained much lower than from Ontonagon. Angler reports included catches of lake trout in fair-to-low numbers. Anglers trolled across depths varying from 60 to 150 feet to find fish.

Angling effort remained low from the harbor over the past week. Anglers caught lake trout in low-to-fair numbers while trolling in depths of 60 to 160 feet. Shore anglers fishing within the harbor boundaries reported catches of smallmouth bass and white suckers in low numbers.

Early salmon began to show, with low numbers moving into the Carp River and a handful staging at Nunns Creek. Anglers targeting their first fall-run salmon of the season cast spoons and drifted spawn.
Weather conditions limited fishing activity. When weather permitted, boat anglers reported doing well when targeting lake trout trolling and jigging at deeper depths.

Anglers reported good Chinook salmon fishing from the "green can" buoy located south of Manistique to Fairport. Anglers had good success trolling in water depths of 100 to 150 feet of water. Magnum-sized spoons were productive. Anglers who fished near the mouth of the Manistique River reported slow fishing, as did pier anglers.

Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks out toward Granite Island and the Clay Banks in 80 to 160 feet of water targeting lake trout. Anglers reported catching fish throughout the water column with no clear pattern. A few anglers reported catching salmon and brown trout near Little Presque Isle and the Clay Banks area around Granite Island and the Little Garlic River in 60 to 100 feet of water. Few anglers headed out to the Sand River or Shot Point, with lower numbers of lake trout reported. Coho salmon were caught in 60 feet of water between the Lower Harbor Lighthouse and the Chocolay River, with lines set 25 to 30 feet down.

Anglers reported catching lake trout, along with a few coho salmon, splake, and Chinook salmon, while trolling spoons and flasher-fly rigs over the past week. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite, finding success on both natural and artificial presentations. Fish were caught in 100 to 140 feet of water.
Fishing activity remained slow with most anglers targeting Walleye and Yellow Perch. Anglers did best jigging in 10 to 15 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers reported fair-to-good fishing for lake trout while trolling spoons and flasher-fly rigs near the bottom in 90 to 120 feet of water and around structure. Coho salmon, steelhead, and a few brown trout were also caught in low numbers while trolling. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite when using natural and artificial baits, with most fish caught between 100 and 140 feet of water and some caught in depths near 200 feet.

Ask many anglers and they’ll tell you fall is a wonderful time to go fishing as fish prepare for the colder months by ramping up their feeding efforts. Most will target salmon, walleye, perch, panfish and bass and see much success when doing so.
Many fish will return very hungry to their natal streams throughout this month. Check out Michigan.gov/FishID on the DNR’s website for tips on spots to locate them.

Large schools of this species will move from the Great Lakes inland. By the end of September these fish will really be biting. Visit Michigan.gov/Walleye to learn more about techniques for targeting them.

Both Lake Michigan and Lake Erie provide great opportunities for perch fishing during the fall as the large schools head to shallow water. Check out Michigan.gov/FishID to find some great spots to fish for them.
This report is intended to give you an idea of what is going on around the state. Updates come from Fisheries staff and conservation officers. With nearly 11,000 inland lakes, the Great Lakes and thousands of miles of rivers and streams, not all locations can be listed. However, it is safe to say if a species is being caught in some waters in the area, they are likely being caught in all waters in that section of the state that have that species.
Fishing was slow with very anglers seen. There was reports of walleye caught on the east side of Spoils Island in 10 feet of water using crawlers.

Windy conditions and rain contributed to slow fishing across most areas. A few walleye were caught trolling nightcrawler harnesses in 16 feet of water in the slot off Sunset Marina. A few yellow perch were also caught in the same area.
High winds and limited boat ramp access contributed to slow fishing. Pier fishing was also restricted due to beach-level access closures.

High winds limited angling activity. Pier anglers saw steady activity with variable success targeting bass and northern pike off the breakwall using both live bait and artificial lures. Boat anglers reported some success trolling for steelhead in 140 feet of water, though fishing was generally slow overall.
Windy conditions throughout the week resulted in slow fishing. Pier anglers targeting smallmouth bass had limited success, while anglers targeting salmon off the breakwall reported no catches.
Recreational boaters accounted for the majority of on-water activity. Both pier anglers and those fishing Bird Creek reported slow action, with few fish caught.

Southerly winds warmed the water and pushed down the thermocline. Boat anglers found salmon 70 to 130 feet down in 140 to 200 feet of water. Green and blue spoons were effective, along with green flies fished deeper in the water column. Pier anglers targeting salmon reported slow fishing due to warmer water conditions.

Water temperatures warmed over the past few days, causing salmon to move offshore and hold deeper in the water column. The best action for boat anglers occurred 65 to 130 feet down in 150 to 220 feet of water. White flasher-fly combinations was effective deep in the water column. Pier anglers targeting salmon reported very slow action due to increased water temperatures. A few freshwater drum were caught by anglers casting spoons.
Fishing was slow but panfish were caught on inland lakes. The Grand River produced smallmouth bass, walleye, and panfish.

Walleye fishing slowed, with boat anglers averaging zero to five fish. Other anglers targeting yellow perch had mixed success. A few boat anglers caught larger perch off Au Gres in approximately 40 feet of water. Perch were also caught off Standish, though most were undersized.

Anglers reported walleye remained scattered in 20 to 40 feet of water. Near Sulphur Island, anglers had some success trolling crawler harnesses on leadcore line, as well as deep-diving crankbaits. Anglers also reported success targeting walleye in 30 to 50 feet of water near North Point using crankbaits and leadcore line. A few Chinook salmon and coho salmon were caught while trolling spoons in 30 to 50 feet of water. The best results came from medium-sized spoons in green and white, chartreuse, and black patterns.

Anglers reported a few Chinook salmon were caught near the 9th Street Dam while casting crankbaits. A few walleye were also caught on crankbaits and small spinners. Boat anglers reported slow action, with only a few northern pike and smallmouth bass caught.

Anglers reported walleye fishing as variable. Anglers that had success used deep-diving crankbaits and crawler harnesses in 20 to 50 feet of water. Anglers targeting salmon reported abundant baitfish in the area, though only a few Chinook salmon were caught. Lake trout were caught in 80 to 130 feet of water. Spin-N-Glos and spoons were effective when trolled near the bottom.

In the Cheboygan River, Chinook salmon, walleye, smallmouth bass, rock bass, and yellow perch were caught. Early in the morning and at sunset, low numbers of Chinook salmon were caught at the Cheboygan pier and the Cheboygan Dam spillway. At the pier, salmon were caught on spoons. At the dam, salmon were caught drifting spawn and casting spoons and minnow-style crankbaits. Anglers trolling for salmon near the river mouth harvested up to two fish per boat using spoons, J-plugs, and flasher-fly combinations. An occasional walleye and smallmouth bass were caught incidentally while casting spoons for salmon. Rock bass, smallmouth bass, and yellow perch were caught drifting nightcrawlers between the Cheboygan Dam and the pedestrian bridge.

Salmon staged off Swan Bay, providing a variable bite. Overall catch rates remained low, though fish were present in the area. The most productive fishing occurred before sunrise, after sunset, or on overcast days. Productive depths ranged from 30 to 90 feet of water depending on conditions, with salmon holding shallower in low-light hours. Spreading lines throughout the water column produced the best results.
Anglers trolled standard spoons and magnum spoons, J-plugs, and meat rigs. Flasher-fly combinations and squids were also successful. Effective colors included green, blue, chartreuse, orange, white, black, and UV patterns, with glow presentations working best early and late in the day. Walleye were occasionally caught as incidental catches.
Anglers venturing outside the Swan Bay area caught lake trout, along with a few steelhead and coho salmon. Lake trout were caught near the bottom in colder water, while steelhead and coho salmon held higher in the water column.

Fishing improved though angler effort remained low. Anglers fishing between the lighthouses or south toward Stoneport caught a mixed bag of lake trout, along with the occasional salmon and walleye. Productive depths ranged from 45 to 90 feet of water, with fish caught throughout the water column. Both standard and magnum spoons produced fish. Anglers also had success running flasher-fly and flasher-squid combinations. Effective colors included green, blue, orange, chartreuse, black, purple, white, UV, and glow patterns early and late in the day.

A few chinook salmon were caught off the pier, in the channel, and in Manistee Lake by anglers jigging and trolling. Anglers trolling off the piers also caught Chinook salmon using plugs and spoons in 30 to 40 feet of water. Warm water from southerly winds slowed the bite. Anglers fishing along the shelf, both north and south of Manistee, caught a mix of Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead in 70 to 150 feet of water while trolling 45 to 60 feet down with spoons, plugs, and flies, though the bite was variable.

Windy weather throughout the week kept most boat anglers off Lake Michigan. Early in the week, Chinook salmon were caught by anglers jigging, drifting eggs, or trolling in Pere Marquette Lake and the channel. Warm water in the area slowed the bite in the harbor and on Lake Michigan. Pier fishing was slow.

Anglers targeting salmon reported low numbers of Chinook salmon and the occasional steelhead. Trolling 60 to 90 feet down in over 120 feet of water produced fish on spoons, flasher-fly combinations, plugs, and meat rigs. An occasional lake trout was also caught.

Boat anglers reported low numbers of salmon on both sides of the bay. Trolling 60 to 90 feet down in over 100 feet of water produced fair results. Catches consisted mostly of Chinook salmon, along with the occasional coho salmon, steelhead, and lake trout. A few fish moved into the Bear River.

Anglers fishing out of Elk Rapids caught lake trout and chinook salmon while trolling approximately 80 to 90 feet down in 100 to 140 feet of water. Cowbells, along with white and green flasher-fly combinations, were effective. Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught both lake trout and salmon while trolling in 80 to 140 feet of water. Water temperatures throughout the bay hovered between 70 and 73 degrees.
Chinook salmon were caught by anglers trolling around the mouth of the Boardman River in 80 to 120 feet of water. A mix of plugs, spoons, and flasher-fly combinations was effective.

Wind over the weekend kept some anglers off the water, as cooler water conditions were still reported. Anglers fishing out front and, in the Herring Hole, reported good catches during the morning and late evening bites. Plugs generated more action in 90 to 140 feet of water. Pier anglers reported moderate numbers of Chinook salmon and coho salmon during the overnight hours and early morning. Overnight anglers cast glow spoons and caught alewives for bait. Chinook salmon began to darken in color as they staged for the river run. Anglers jigging the harbor and channel reported catching Chinook salmon.

Anglers fishing the Barrel and off the golf course in 100 to 140 feet of water reported catching Chinook salmon and coho salmon while trolling spoons and plugs in the early morning, then moving to deeper water as the sun rose.
Panfish fishing was excellent across the chain, with multiple anglers catching limits of large bluegill from both shore and boats.
Bass and panfish fishing was very good. Anglers reported good bass action after sunrise. Some limits of quality bluegill were caught, and anglers targeting northern pike landed a few fair-sized fish.
Walleye fishing was good in the late evening. Bluegill and rock bass were caught in good numbers below Rogers Dam.
Fishing was very good from kayaks and shore. Anglers caught multiple panfish and bass, with most effort focused in the channels.
Anglers reported success targeting smallmouth bass on the Muskegon River downstream from Croton Dam. Inland lakes produced good catches of panfish and bass.

Lake Michigan produced limits of Chinook salmon from Little Sable Point to the Silver Lake Sand Dunes. An upwelling event dropped water temperatures from 70 to 50 degrees. In addition, anglers caught Chinook salmon inside the Pentwater channel.

Anglers reported fair to good walleye fishing over the past week. Anglers used sonar to locate fish and cast minnow-profile baits. Presentations varied from erratic reaction-style lures to slow-moving live bait, including nightcrawlers on crawler harnesses or jigs. Anglers also caught coho salmon near the mouth of the Escanaba River while trolling or casting spoons and small crankbaits.

Angling effort on the river was low. Anglers reported fair numbers of walleye caught while jigging, while trolling remained a less effective method. Early morning hours produced the most successful trips.

Angling effort out of Ontonagon was low over the past week, with even lower effort observed from the Silver City and Union Bay access sites. Angler reports indicated fair catches of lake trout. Anglers reported trolling across depths ranging from 50 to 150 feet of water to find fish.

The harbor continued to see low angling effort. Boat anglers reported fair to low catches of lake trout. Reports indicated fish were caught while trolling in depths of 50 to 150 feet of water. A few anglers fishing within the harbor boundaries reported low numbers of white suckers.
Low numbers of Chinook salmon were reported at the mouths of the Carp River and Nunns Creek. Anglers caught up to one salmon per boat while casting spoons or drifting spawn at both locations.

Anglers fishing near the river mouth reported slow chinook salmon fishing. Despite marking fish on sonar, bites were rare. Anglers heading away from the mouth of the river and targeting staging salmon reported good fishing while trolling spoons. Few adult Chinook salmon were caught near the Garden Peninsula, though overall catch rates remained good.

Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks out toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks in 80 to 160 feet of water for lake trout. Anglers reported catching fish throughout the water column. A few anglers reported catching salmon and brown trout near Little Presque Isle and the Clay Banks around Granite Point and the Little Garlic River in 60 to 100 feet of water. Few anglers ventured out to the Sand River and Shot Point, resulting in low numbers of lake trout, though fish were caught in deeper water near the sand hole in around 180 feet of water. Coho salmon were caught between the Lower Harbor Lighthouse and the Chocolay River in 60 feet of water, with lines set 25 to 30 feet down. The South Shore Fishing Tournament yielded few salmon.

A few anglers fished out of Au Train. Commercial net presence decreased in the area, which saw low fishing pressure overall throughout the summer. Anglers targeted the flats northeast of Au Train Island in 120 to 160 feet of water. Lake trout were caught near the bottom using chartreuse Spin-N-Glo lures.

Anglers reported catching primarily lake trout, with the occasional coho salmon trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a poor to fair bite, with success on both natural and artificial presentations. Fish were caught in 100 to 140 feet of water, with some anglers catching smaller fish in water deeper than 200 feet.
Fishing activity remained slow with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers did best jigging in 10 to 15 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers reported fair to good fishing for lake trout while trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations near the bottom in 60 to 100 feet of water and around structure. Coho salmon and a few brown trout were also caught in low numbers while trolling. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite when using natural presentations, with most fish caught between 100 and 140 feet of water with a few caught in water deeper than 200 feet.

Anglers in Hessel caught yellow perch off the pier at the marina. Perch of various sizes were present in good numbers throughout the area, with minnows proving to be the most productive bait. Anglers also caught smallmouth bass around the marina using jigs and soft plastics as the fish schooled up and grew more aggressive. Lake trout were caught while trolling and jigging in the middle and west entrances. In DeTour, conditions were extremely windy. However, when anglers made it out, they did well catching lake trout and picked up a few pink salmon.

Atlantic salmon and lake whitefish fishing was extremely slow in Sault Ste. Marie over the summer, leading to minimal angling effort in the area. Anglers targeting walleye throughout the St. Marys River reported improved success near the shipping channel and around the north side of Drummond Island.

Targeting walleye in the fall can offer some of the best fishing of the season. Here are a few things to keep in mind if you target this sportfish in the near future.
Learn more about fishing for walleye in Michigan at Michigan.gov/Walleye .
This report is intended to give you an idea of what is going on around the state. Updates come from Fisheries staff and conservation officers. With nearly 11,000 inland lakes, the Great Lakes and thousands of miles of rivers and streams, not all locations can be listed. However, it is safe to say if a species is being caught in some waters in the area, they are likely being caught in all waters in that section of the state that have that species.
Fishing was slow with very anglers seen. There was reports of walleye caught on the east side of Spoils Island in 10 feet of water using crawlers.

Yellow perch began schooling east of Stony Point. Some anglers caught fair numbers in approximately 18 feet of water before moving into deeper water. Perch rigs dressed with feathers and beads tipped with minnows were effective, with red producing the best results. Emerald shiners were in short supply, though other minnow species proved effective. Catches consisted of many small yellow perch, though larger fish did appear in the area. Walleye moved back across the state line into deeper waters on the Ohio side.
Boat anglers caught a few 9 to 11-inch yellow perch at sailboat buoys B and F, along with numerous 5 to 7-inch fish. Some boat anglers kept approximately 15 to 20 yellow perch per boat.

Fishing was very slow across all access points over the past week. Water temperatures remained warm, with surface temperatures reported in the mid-70s. Anglers caught a few walleye near the Spark Plug midweek while trolling nightcrawler harnesses. Action remained slow overall, with cooler temperatures expected to improve fishing conditions.

Boat anglers reported fair numbers of salmon 65 to 110 feet down in 90 to 150 feet of water. A white flasher and green fly combination was effective, along with glow spoons and plugs. Pier anglers were unsuccessful targeting salmon due to warm water temperatures.

Salmon action was good for boat anglers 65 to 100 feet down in 85 to 140 feet of water. Green and white flies were effective. Pier anglers had success catching largemouth bass on drop-shot and Ned rigs. No salmon were reported from the pier by anglers casting spoons.

Pier fishing was slow, though a few steelhead were caught by anglers casting spoons. Salmon anglers reported fair fishing, though rough lake conditions kept most boat anglers from reaching the most productive waters which were beyond 120 feet. A few salmon were caught inside 100 feet of water. Yellow perch anglers caught a few quality fish. Fishing remained inconsistent, depths around 45 feet of water had the most success.

Pier fishing was slow for all species. Boat anglers targeting salmon caught fair numbers of fish, though rough weather conditions made it difficult for boat anglers to reach productive waters. The best bite occurred in around 120 feet of water. Yellow perch anglers reported good catches. Schools moved frequently, but depths around 40 feet of water were most productive.

Windy conditions kept many boat anglers off the water. When anglers were able to get out, fishing was slow overall. Anglers targeting walleye averaged 0 to 4 fish per boat, while those targeting yellow perch also returned with low catches. Shore anglers at the mouth of the Tawas River and at the state dock in Tawas caught primarily largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, and rock bass.

A few walleye were caught in 20 to 30 feet of water while trolling nightcrawlers and deep-diving crankbaits near North Point and Sulphur Island. Anglers reported lake trout and a few Chinook salmon caught in 70 to 120 feet of water straight out of Thunder Bay. Flashers paired with Spin-N-Glos and spoons were productive fished near the bottom, with white, chartreuse, and blue patterns working best. A few Chinook salmon were also caught in the middle of the water column on spoons and plugs in green, black and green, and orange.

A few Chinook salmon were caught near the Ninth Street Bridge on glow spoons during low-light conditions. Anglers reported slow fishing overall. A few smallmouth bass and northern pike were caught on leeches and small spinners.

Walleye were caught in 20 to 40 feet of water near Middle Island. Anglers reported fair catches while trolling nightcrawlers and crankbaits. Lake trout fishing was very good for anglers targeting 80 to 120 feet of water. Flashers paired with Spin-N-Glos along with spoons in white, chartreuse, and watermelon produced the best results. A few Chinook salmon were caught near False Presque Isle in 60 to 90 feet of water. Plugs, spoons, and cut bait yielded mixed results early and late in the day.

Chinook salmon were seen surfacing at the Cheboygan pier and the Cheboygan Dam spillway at daybreak and nightfall, though catch rates slowed. An occasional Chinook salmon was caught while trolling J-plugs and spoons between the buoy markers and the fish cleaning station. From the pier, salmon were caught periodically on small spoons. At the Cheboygan Dam spillway, anglers had success drifting spawn or casting spoons and minnow-style crankbaits. Small walleye, smallmouth bass, and rock bass were caught while drifting nightcrawlers between the Cheboygan Dam and the pedestrian walkway bridge.

Anglers targeting lake trout had good success in 120 to 140 feet of water while trolling spoons in the bottom 20 feet of the water column. Steelhead and a few chinook salmon were caught in 80 to 120 feet of water. Anglers fishing from the pier and catwalk had good success catching channel catfish using nightcrawlers on the bottom. A few walleye were caught by anglers casting deep-diving crankbaits at dusk.

Anglers targeting lake trout in 115 to 140 feet of water had good success on spoons and Spin-N-Glos. A few steelhead were also caught on spoons fished higher in the water column. Anglers casting spinners in the harbor caught a few northern pike.

Salmon were staging off Swan Bay, though the bite was inconsistent. Overall numbers remained low, with the best action occurring before sunrise, after sunset, or on overcast days. Productive depths ranged from 30 to 90 feet of water depending on the day, with fish moving shallower early in the morning and after dark. Trolling lines throughout the water column produced the best results. Anglers used standard and magnum spoons, J-plugs, and meat rigs. Flasher-fly combinations and squids also took fish. Productive colors included green, blue, chartreuse, orange, white, black, and UV patterns, with glow lures being effective early and late in the day. Walleye were caught as incidental catches. Anglers venturing outside the Swan Bay area caught lake trout, along with incidental steelhead and coho salmon. Lake trout were caught in colder water near the bottom, while steelhead and coho salmon were found higher in the water column.

Fishing improved, though angling effort remained low. Anglers fishing between the lighthouses or south toward Stoneport caught a mixed bag of lake trout, along with an occasional salmon or walleye. Productive depths ranged from 45 to 90 feet of water, with lines spread throughout the water column producing the best results. Standard and magnum spoons caught fish, and anglers also ran flasher-fly and squid combinations. Productive colors included green, blue, orange, chartreuse, black, purple, white, and UV patterns, with effective glow patterns early and late in the day.

Anglers targeting Chinook salmon caught fish along the shelf in 90 to 200 feet of water while trolling 60 to 90-plus feet down with plugs, spoons, and flies. A few coho salmon and steelhead were also caught. Very few Chinook salmon were caught outside the pierheads in 35 feet of water while trolling plugs. Warm water temperatures kept pier fishing slow.

Warm water remained in the area. Pier anglers experienced no salmon action over the weekend. Trolling boats had limited success off Big Sable Point when fishing in 135 to 200 feet of water, 70 to 90-plus feet down with plugs, spoons, flasher-fly combinations, and meat rigs. Salmon were also caught straight out in 85 to 180 feet of water while fishing 55 to 70-plus feet down. Boats heading south caught a few fish in 120 to 140 feet of water, 80 to 90 feet down. Catches consisted mostly of Chinook salmon, with a few coho salmon and steelhead mixed in.

Boat anglers reported warm water temperatures, with the thermocline located 75 to 90 feet down with abundant baitfish in the area. Anglers fishing from the pier reported an occasional legal-size smallmouth bass caught on nightcrawlers and other natural bait.

Anglers fishing the Bear River reported a slow but steady run of salmon entering the river system. Boat anglers trolling the bay reported abundant baitfish scattered throughout the area. Water temperatures in the bay remained warm over the past week, with anglers locating the thermocline 75 to 85 feet down.

Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught both salmon and lake trout while trolling in 110 to 140 feet of water. Spoons, plugs, and flasher-fly combinations were all effective. Anglers trolling out of Elk Rapids in 100 to 160 feet of water caught lake trout, with a few chinook salmon mixed in. Water temperatures throughout the bay ranged from 70 to 73 degrees.

Lake trout were caught by anglers trolling in 120 to 160 feet of water along the west bank just north of Elmwood Marina. Anglers trolling near the mouth of the Boardman River also caught a few Chinook salmon, though action was slow due to warm water temperatures. Surface water temperatures ranged from 69 to 73 degrees throughout the bay.

Anglers targeting Chinook salmon reported fair catches. Successful boat anglers trolled north from the docks on North Manitou Island in depths of 150 to 300 feet of water, running lures 60 to 125 feet down. Green presentations, including plugs, spoons, and flies, were effective.
Anglers fishing around the Crib caught a few coho salmon. Fish moved closer to shore, trolling north along the first and second banks were successful for anglers targeting chinook salmon. Pier fishing was slow.

Chinook salmon were caught out deep on the bank in the early morning and closer to shore during the evening. Anglers reported good numbers caught on spoons and plugs. Anglers jigging in the harbor reported moderate success using jigging spoons and skein. Anglers fishing Platte Bay reported very good catches of coho salmon while drifting skein near the bottom in 40 to 80 feet of water.

Anglers trolling in 180 to 220 feet of water in front of the golf course and the barrel reported a few Chinook salmon were caught on spoons in the early morning hours. Numbers slowed down as the warm water kept Chinook salmon in deeper water.

Anglers targeted Chinook salmon and lake trout. Anglers trolling north out of Suttons Bay along the shoreline toward Omena Bay caught a few Chinook salmon. Lake trout were caught while jigging near Stony Point and Omena Bay. Water temperatures were reported in the mid-60s.

Walleye fishing was good, with anglers targeting reefs and nearby drop-offs. Trolling slowly near the bottom with crawler harnesses was the most effective method. Yellow perch anglers reported fair to good fishing, though action varied from day to day, with schools located in 20 feet of water or deeper. Coho salmon anglers reported a few fish in the river. Morning hours were the most productive, though the overall bite for coho salmon remained slow, with only a few boats recording productive trips while trolling standard-sized spoons or crankbaits.

Boat anglers reported good success jigging and trolling for lake trout around Grand Island and Wood Island. Salmon action was slow for trolling boat anglers, though a few splake were caught in the bay. Anglers fishing off the mouth of the Anna River reported slow splake action, with only a few fish caught. Spawn and spoons were the most effective presentations.

Angling effort on the river increased slightly over the past week and during the holiday weekend. Anglers caught walleye in low to fair numbers while jigging. Trolling was not an effective method for locating fish. Fishing was productive during the early morning hours.

Angling effort out of Ontonagon increased slightly over the past week. Effort from the Silver City and Union Bay access sites also increased, though it remained lower than that observed in Ontonagon. Anglers reported fair catches of lake trout with lower numbers of coho salmon. Successful boat anglers trolled in depths ranging from 50 to 150 feet of water.

The harbor saw a slight increase in angling effort over the holiday weekend. Anglers reported catches of brown trout, steelhead, coho salmon, and lake trout in low to fair numbers. Lake trout remained the most common catch. Anglers caught fish while trolling in depths ranging from 50 to 150 feet of water.

Although fishing pressure increased at the Carp River, catch rates remained very low for Chinook salmon. The few successful anglers caught fish casting small glow spoons before daybreak and at nightfall.
Boat anglers had good success catching lake trout while trolling and jigging. Anglers reported slow salmon action.

Anglers reported fair fishing near the river mouth. A few salmon were reported in the river, though the primary run for salmon is yet to be seen. Anglers trolling in deeper water near the Garden Peninsula or south of Manistique reported fair catches of salmon. Most mature fish were seen moving toward river systems.

Most anglers trolled north of White Rocks toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks in 80 to 160 feet of water for lake trout. Anglers reported catching lake trout throughout the water column with no consistent pattern. A few anglers reported catching salmon and brown trout near Little Presque Isle, the Clay Banks, Granot Loma, and the Little Garlic River in 60 to 100 feet of water, though action was slow overall. Angling effort remained low off the Sand River and Shot Point, where lake trout numbers were low except in deeper water near the Sand Hole in approximately 180 feet of water.

Angling effort out of Au Train increased substantially over the past week following low fishing pressure throughout the summer, with catch rates reflecting the improvement. On Saturday, many boat anglers caught bag limits of lake trout. Boat anglers targeted depths similar to previous weeks, working 140 to 180 feet of water along the Flats northeast of Au Train Island and west of the Wood Island Reef. All lake trout were caught near the bottom. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in shallower depths of 40 to 60 feet of water reported marking high concentrations of fish on sonar, though the fish did not bite.

Anglers reported fair fishing, with catches consisting primarily of lake trout along with an occasional coho salmon or brown trout. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair to poor bite, with fish taken on both natural and artificial presentations. Most catches occurred in approximately 150 feet of water, though some boats reported success in depths greater than 200 feet.
Fishing activity increased, with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers had the best success while trolling in 10 to 15 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers reported fair to good fishing when targeting lake trout while trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations around structure in 50 to 100 feet of water. A few coho salmon were also caught while trolling nearshore waters or around river mouths. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite using natural presentations, with most fish caught in 100 to 140 feet of water and some success reported in depths greater than 200 feet.

With the colder months quickly approaching, many anglers may be getting ready to store their gear for the season. Below are a few maintenance tips you should follow so your gear is cared for and ready to be used next season.
This report is intended to give you an idea of what is going on around the state. Updates come from Fisheries staff and conservation officers. With nearly 11,000 inland lakes, the Great Lakes and thousands of miles of rivers and streams, not all locations can be listed. However, it is safe to say if a species is being caught in some waters in the area, they are likely being caught in all waters in that section of the state that have that species.

Boat anglers caught approximately 30 good-sized yellow perch per vessel over the weekend in Michigan waters, potentially marking the start of their seasonal return. Anglers fished east of Stony Point near the Ohio border using minnows on perch rigs. Water temperatures continued to drop, which should improve conditions. Virtually no walleye were caught over the past week as fish remained in deeper water. Largemouth bass were active along submerged cover.
Yellow perch and walleye fishing was poor due to northeast winds, with only a few yellow perch and walleye caught in the lower Saginaw River.

High winds kept fishing effort to a minimum in many areas. A few yellow perch were caught in the slot off Fish Point, though numbers were low. Anglers fished half-day trips to keep five to eight fish, with extensive sorting required. Northern pike were also caught by anglers casting various artificial lures in the Quanicassee River. Elsewhere, fishing activity and effort remained slow.

Overall fishing was slow. Pier anglers tried fishing off the rocky south pier at the boat launch without success. A few boat anglers caught yellow perch inside the harbor using bobbers and minnows. The north pier remained inaccessible, and the boat launch continued to operate with only one working dock.

Silver fish began to appear nearshore, with a few anglers reporting coho salmon and steelhead off the north and south breakwalls. Spoons, spinners, and spawn were effective, though the movement of salmon and trout remained relatively slow. Some anglers caught northern pike and smallmouth bass off the south breakwall using spinners. Boat fishing remained slow, with few fish caught. Access along the inside of the north breakwall was limited due to dredging.

Anglers caught coho salmon off the pier. A few anglers had success using spoons and spinners when targeting coho salmon, with many caught along the inside wall of the harbor. Water conditions were murky but showed signs of clearing. Windy conditions limited boat angling activity while pier anglers benefited.

Boat anglers reported fair salmon action 25 to 80 feet down in 70 to 140 feet of water. Spoons in green, blue, and orange worked well. The south breakwall in Muskegon is closed due to lighthouse repairs.

Boat anglers found immature Chinook salmon, steelhead, and a few lake trout 30 to 80 feet down in 60 to 180 feet of water. Spoons were most productive in green and orange. Pier anglers reported slow salmon action, though a few mature salmon were caught using glow spoons, alewives, and gizzard shad. The north pier in Grand Haven is closed, with a projected reopening in the summer of 2028.

Pier fishing was slow for all species, with only an occasional Chinook salmon or steelhead caught. Boat anglers had good success targeting salmon in around 60 feet of water using plugs and spoons. No perch reports were received.

Fishing pressure remained high on the piers, though fishing was slow for all species. A handful of salmon and steelhead were caught by anglers casting spoons or crankbaits. Boat anglers continued to catch a few fish around the pierheads, with better fishing reported in around 60 feet of water using spoons. Perch fishing was fair, with fish scattered in 40 to 60 feet of water.
Salmon fishing was slow in the lower river. Salmon were present in the area, but fishing was difficult. Some salmon caught near the Berrien Springs Dam.
Salmon fishing slowed in the river. A few fish were still caught while trolling, though action was overall slow.

Wind kept most boat anglers off the water. The anglers who were able to fish reported slow fishing when targeting walleye and yellow perch. Coho salmon and Chinook salmon were caught in the Tawas River on spawn and various artificial baits.

Boat anglers targeting 40 to 60 feet of water had some success on lake trout, along with a few Atlantic salmon and coho salmon. Fish were still well scattered throughout the water column. A few walleye were also caught using standard-sized spoons on leadcore and downriggers. Anglers reported slow Chinook salmon action, with only a few fish caught.

While anglers reported seeing both coho salmon and Chinook salmon, the catch rate was low. Anglers who found success drifted spawn and beads. Casting glow spoons produced a few fish after dark. A few Atlantic salmon were caught while casting spinners and drifting beads.

Anglers targeting lake trout had success in 55 to 100 feet of water on spoons, flashers, and Spin-N-Glos. With cold water moving in, the majority of fish were caught in the top 40 feet of water. A few salmon were caught in the same depth on medium-sized spoons. Walleye anglers reported slow fishing, with only a few fish caught. Pier anglers had no success.

Anglers at the Cheboygan Dam spillway caught low numbers of Chinook salmon, along with an occasional coho salmon, pink salmon, or steelhead. A handful of Chinook salmon were caught at the Cheboygan pier. Salmon and trout were caught when casting small spoons or minnow-style crankbaits, as well as drifted or bottom-bounced beads and spawn.
Small walleye, smallmouth bass, and rock bass were also caught between the Cheboygan Dam and State Street drawbridge while drifting nightcrawlers.

Boat anglers trolling spoons early in the morning caught a few coho salmon and Atlantic salmon off the pierhead in 15 to 30 feet of water. A few Chinook salmon were also caught on spoons and J-plugs. Anglers casting from the pier found similar success, catching a few coho salmon and Chinook salmon while casting spoons, spinners, and body baits early in the morning. Blue and silver, orange, and green were popular spoon colors, while fire-tiger and clown were effective patterns for body baits such as Bandits or J-13s. Anglers casting body baits or jigheads with split-tail plastics off the pier caught walleye at dusk.

Anglers targeting coho salmon and Chinook salmon in the harbor found limited success while casting spoons, spinners, and Jr. thundersticks. A few salmon were caught this week along with a steelhead, with dawn and dusk being the most productive times.

Adult Chinook salmon were present in 20 to 30 feet of water off Swan Bay. Anglers trolled plugs and Bombers off planar boards. Lake trout and immature Chinook salmon, along with the occasional steelhead, coho salmon, and walleye, were caught outside of the bay or straight out from the harbor. Lines were set throughout the water column near baitfish. Spoons were the most effective choice, with standard-sized and slim-profile models performing best. Effective lure colors included white, green, blue, orange, yellow, and glow patterns during early morning and late evening hours.

Anglers were sparse due to rough and windy weather conditions. When boat anglers were able to get out, lake trout were caught off Stoneport and between the lighthouses. An occasional Chinook salmon was caught off Stoneport, False Presque Isle, and off the Grand River outlet north of the marina. Steelhead, coho salmon, and walleye were caught incidentally. The most productive depths ranged from 45 to 80 feet of water, with lines set throughout the water column. Anglers trolled a mix of J-Plugs and spoons. Effective lure colors included white, green, blue, orange, and glow patterns during early morning and late evening hours.

Anglers targeting salmon reported slow fishing. A few fish were caught just outside the pierheads and in Manistee Lake by boat anglers trolling plugs and jigging spoons. Pier fishing was fair for anglers targeting Chinook salmon and coho salmon while casting spoons. Anglers fishing along the shelf reported a few Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead in the top 40 feet of water in 150 to 200 feet of water. Fish were caught using spoons and plugs in glow, purple, and orange colors.

Pier fishing was very slow, though a few salmon were caught during late night hours. Boat anglers trolling for chinook salmon caught a limited number in the channel, in the harbor, and straight out in 50 to 80 feet of water. Salmon and a few steelhead were also caught to the northwest in 60 to 80 feet of water, as well as in 60 to 140 feet of water at and around Big Sauble Point in the top 40 feet of water using spoons and plugs. Steelhead were caught on orange colors.

Water temperatures cooled significantly over the past week, with the temperature break holding near 35 feet down. Boat anglers trolling reported inconsistent salmon catches throughout the week. Chinook salmon were found 40 to 80 feet down in more than 80 feet of water, while an occasional coho salmon was caught in the upper 40 feet. Anglers targeting fish near Medusa Creek reported slow but steady action early in the morning while drifting skein or casting and trolling body baits.

Boat anglers targeting salmon reported slow action near the end of the Petoskey breakwall while trolling in roughly 30 feet of water. Anglers casting spoons and body baits off the pier and Clock Dock reported steady results. Anglers targeting salmon in the Bear River reported catches on flies and skein. An occasional steelhead was caught while drifting the river and trolling from boats.

Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught lake trout along with a few Chinook salmon when trolling in 80 to 140 feet of water. A mix of plugs and spoons worked well. A few cisco were caught around Old Mission roughly 50 to 70 feet down in 90 to 120 feet of water.

Lake trout along with a few Chinook salmon were caught by boat anglers trolling in 120 to 150 feet of water along the west bank just north of Elmwood Marina. A mix of spoons and flasher-fly combinations worked well. Boat anglers trolling near the Red 6 Buoy in 100 to 120 feet of water caught a few lake trout. Anglers caught salmon while trolling in 100 to 125 feet of water near the mouth of the Boardman River.

Anglers targeted Chinook salmon on the First Bank in 100 to 300 feet of water. Water temperature was reported to be 42 degrees from the surface down to 100 feet of water. Fishing was sporadic with no thermocline present. Anglers targeted all portions of the water column, catching coho salmon and Chinook salmon in 30 to 60 feet of water on blue and orange trolling spoons. Lake trout fishing was productive in 100 to 120 feet of water using attractors such as cowbells fished directly on the bottom. Pier anglers had the best success catching Chinook salmon before sunrise while drifting skein.

Cooler water moved into the area along with Chinook salmon and coho salmon. Chinook salmon continued to move into the Betsie River in lower numbers, with anglers reporting good action in deeper holes. Pier anglers casting spoons and rigging alewives reported very good fishing during late evening and early morning hours. Boat anglers trolling offshore in the early morning and evening reported good numbers of 2-year-old Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and an occasional steelhead.
Anglers trolling the channel and just out front of the light house reported a few coho salmon caught on spoons in the early morning hours.
Boat anglers targeted yellow perch throughout Suttons Bay, Omena Bay, and Northport, though few anglers reported success when using natural bait.

Anglers targeting coho salmon fished the Escanaba River. Anglers reported seeing fish surface in the river and near the dam. Fishing was slow, with most anglers unable to entice bites. Anglers drifted spawn and cast brightly colored lures. Anglers noted that the run was slowing down, though additional heavy rainfall could bring in remaining coho salmon. Walleye anglers reported fair fishing, with success using natural bait trolled on a harness or cast on a jighead, as well as artificial lures such as snap jigs and crankbaits.

Boat anglers caught a few coho salmon while trolling in the bay. Lake trout anglers had success jigging and trolling around Grand Island and Wood Island. Anglers fishing off the mouth of the Anna River caught a few splake and coho salmon. Casting spinners and drifting spawn produced the best results.
Angling effort on the river was very low over the past week. Recent reports indicated occasional catches of walleye in low numbers. Early morning hours were the most productive.

Angling effort from Ontonagon increased over the past week, with effort from the Silver City and Union Bay access sites increasing significantly. Anglers reported mixed catches of lake trout, brown trout, coho salmon, and Chinook salmon in fair numbers. Boat anglers trolling found fish in depths ranging from 30 to 150 feet. Anglers had better success finding salmon when trolling in shallower water.

Angling effort from the harbor increased slightly over the past week. Anglers reported catches of brown trout, coho salmon, Chinook salmon, and lake trout, with lake trout and coho salmon being the most frequently reported. Fish were caught by boat anglers trolling in 30 to 160 feet of water. Anglers had better success targeting salmon when trolling in shallower water.

Anglers reported salmon moving into Nunns Creek and closer to McDonalds Rapids in the Carp River. Anglers casting spoons and drifting spawn from shore at Nunns Creek caught few Chinook salmon. At the Carp River, Chinook salmon and pink salmon were caught using spoons, spinnerbaits, crankbaits, beads, and spawn.

Boat anglers had success targeting lake trout when trolling and jigging. A few coho salmon were caught by boat anglers trolling east of the breakwall. Shore anglers also caught a few coho salmon near the mouth of the Sucker River while casting spoons.

Pink salmon were plentiful in the river. Anglers targeting pink salmon used small crankbaits, spinners, and beads, typically in pink colors. Chinook salmon anglers reported catching fish in holes of fast water above the U.S. Highway 2 bridge. Anglers reported the best success on skein, though other egg patterns also produced fish. Anglers trolling the river reported slow salmon fishing but caught incidental species such as smallmouth bass and northern pike.

Anglers targeted lake trout in 80 to 160 feet of water. Most boat anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks out toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks, as reports from west of the Chocolay River remained dismal. Anglers reported catching lake trout throughout the water column, though most fish were caught near the bottom using downriggers. A few anglers caught lake trout and coho salmon off the lower breakwall early in the morning and before sunset. Anglers trolling the river mouths out of Lower Harbor caught fair numbers of salmon, including both coho salmon and chinook salmon. Brown trout were among the most frequently caught species in both the Chocolay and Carp rivers, along with numerous coho salmon. Following rain and cooler temperatures, fish numbers began to increase as salmon pods staged near the river mouths ahead of the run.

Tribal nets were reset in the flats northwest of Au Train Island toward Five-Mile Point, requiring caution when navigating that area. Wood Island Reef and the waters northwest of Au Train Island toward the Laughing Whitefish River remained open for lake trout fishing, while Au Train Bay to the Laughing Whitefish River remained open for salmon, brown trout, and steelhead. Anglers jigging near the bottom in 40 to 80 feet of water in front of Au Train Island had good success catching lean lake trout. All lake trout taken this week were caught near the bottom while trolling or jigging. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in shallow water marked numerous fish, though few catches were reported. As angler effort increases over the coming weeks, activity is expected to pick up, particularly off river mouths, Scott Falls, and the Laughing Whitefish River area.

Anglers reported fair to good fishing with catches consisting primarily of coho salmon, lake trout, and a few splake while trolling. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported fair action using natural and artificial presentations in 100 to 140 feet of water. Shore anglers reported improved fishing over the past week, with many anglers catching coho salmon.
Fishing activity remained slow, with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers had the best success jigging in 10 to 15 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers reported fair to good lake trout fishing while trolling spoons and flasher-fly rigs around structure in 50 to 100 feet of water. Anglers reported a few coho salmon and steelhead were caught while trolling, but in very low numbers. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported fair fishing using natural presentations, with most fish caught in 80 to 120 feet of water.

Anglers caught yellow perch in Cedarville within Cedarville Bay and Government Bay. Anglers also caught good numbers of larger smallmouth bass around rocky structures near the islands in Hessel. Splake fishing was extremely slow due to warm weather and elevated water temperatures delaying fish movement. In DeTour, anglers targeted walleye with little success but caught yellow perch near Drummond Island. Anglers also caught good numbers of lake trout while trolling the flats prior to the end of the season on Sept. 30.

This report is intended to give you an idea of what is going on around the state. Updates come from Fisheries staff and conservation officers. With nearly 11,000 inland lakes, the Great Lakes and thousands of miles of rivers and streams, not all locations can be listed. However, it is safe to say if a species is being caught in some waters in the area, they are likely being caught in all waters in that section of the state that have that species.
